title: The Diffusion of Emerging Technologies (Module 6 deck)
author: Andres Fortino (course deck, user-supplied)
locator: Slides 18-19 adoption curve; 22 Bass p/q/m; 26 innovation-decision stages; 27 take-off at about 16%; 29 five factors; 32 adopter categories; 34-35 opinion leaders, change agents, change aides; 46-50 chasm and adopter rules; 52-54 16% rule and the 'new' to 'useful' messaging switch; 74 team-project prompt
supports: Rogers' adopter categories (2.5/13.5/34/34/16%), five factors, stages, roles; take-off at critical mass of about 16% ('crosses the chasm'); 'Adopt early only if high pay-off in a short time and willing to abandon it'; 'track ... adoption patterns and only adopt after the technology has crossed'; vendor messaging moving from 'This is new' to 'This is useful' signals crossing. Slide 74 frames the team project around NYU SPS and agentic AI recruiting agents.
does_not_support: Any measurement of agentic AI. The deck is the FA25 version supplied by the student.

title: ET Promethean Technologies FA26, Prep Lab 6
author: Andres Fortino (course deck, user-supplied)
supports: Prep Lab 6: place the technology tentatively on the adoption curve and state the evidence; 'Distinguish evidence that a technology is actually diffusing from evidence that it is merely receiving attention, investment, or publicity.'
does_not_support: Case-specific conclusions.

title: Assignments 3-4 specialist outputs (Innovation and Disruption; Promethean Classification)
author: Minghan Liu
supports: A3: the SPS proposal is a proposed incremental, sustaining process innovation; compare staff-only, simple retrieval and the proposed agent before any pilot. A4: agentic AI is a Breakthrough with an UNRESOLVED Potential-Promethean candidacy; its broad significance should carry Low weight in SPS's present decision.
does_not_support: Independent evidence; prior AI-assisted student analyses used for continuity.

title: 34% of U.S. adults have used ChatGPT, about double the share in 2023
author: Pew Research Center (Sidoti and McClain)
supports: 34% of U.S. adults have ever used ChatGPT (58% of adults under 30); 28% of employed adults have used it for work, up 20 points since 2023.
does_not_support: Agents; organizational use; 'ever used' is not regular use.

title: The Rapid Adoption of Generative AI
author: Alexander Bick, Adam Blandin, David J. Deming
supports: Nearly 40% of U.S. adults 18-64 use generative AI; adoption faster than PCs and the internet; generative AI assists only 1-5% of all work hours.
does_not_support: Agents; organizations; late-2024 data.

title: Microsoft AI Diffusion Report 2025 H2
author: Microsoft AI Economy Institute
supports: Generative AI used by 16.3% of the world's population in H2 2025; 24.7% of the working-age population in the Global North vs 14.1% in the Global South; U.S. 28.3% (rank 24); UAE 64.0%, Singapore 60.9%.
does_not_support: Agents; organizations. Vendor telemetry with adjustments; differs in definition from D1 and D2. Country figures do not transfer to a U.S. peer group.

title: Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users
author: U.S. Census Bureau (Grundy, Breaux, Khatiwoda)
locator: Business Trends and Outlook Survey AI supplement
supports: 19.8% of U.S. businesses reported using AI in any business function in the last two weeks; 17-20% from December 2025 to May 2026; 37% of firms with 250+ employees; Information sector 39.7%. Question broadened in November 2025 from 'producing goods or services' to 'any business function'.
does_not_support: Agents specifically; educational services not reported. Earlier BTOS figures are not directly comparable.

title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
author: McKinsey & Company
type: self-reported global online survey of executives and practitioners
supports: 88% report regular AI use in at least one function; 23% report their organizations are scaling an agentic AI system somewhere; 39% are experimenting with agents; in any given function no more than 10% report scaling agents; agent use most reported in tech/media/telecom and healthcare.
does_not_support: Representativeness: an online survey across company sizes (38% of respondents at firms with more than $1 billion revenue), weighted by national GDP, not a census of firms; 'agentic' is self-defined by respondents; higher education not reported.

title: Gartner Hype Cycle Identifies Top AI Innovations in 2025
author: Gartner (via Business Wire)
supports: AI agents placed at the Peak of Inflated Expectations on the 2025 Hype Cycle for AI.
does_not_support: Measured adoption. A hype position describes attention and expectations, not diffusion.

title: Gartner Predicts Over 40% of Agentic AI Projects Will Be Canceled by End of 2027
author: Gartner
supports: January 2025 poll of 3,412 webinar attendees: 19% significant agentic AI investment, 42% conservative, 31% wait-and-see; over 40% of agentic projects forecast to be cancelled by end-2027; only about 130 of thousands of 'agentic AI' vendors judged real ('agent washing').
does_not_support: Measured adoption; the poll is self-selected.

title: Stack Overflow 2025 Developer Survey press release
author: Stack Overflow
supports: 84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools; 31% currently use AI agents, 17% plan to, 38% do not plan to; 46% distrust AI output accuracy.
does_not_support: Any non-software occupation; developers are lead users, not a proxy for admissions offices.

title: Donating the Model Context Protocol and establishing the Agentic AI Foundation
author: Anthropic
supports: MCP moved to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation (co-founded by Anthropic, Block, OpenAI); 10,000+ active public MCP servers; adopted by ChatGPT, Cursor, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, VS Code: a standards/ecosystem accelerator.
does_not_support: Self-reported counts; organizational adoption.

title: Linux Foundation Launches the Agent2Agent Protocol Project
author: Linux Foundation
supports: Google-created A2A protocol for agent-to-agent communication moved to the Linux Foundation, with support from more than 100 technology companies: a second interoperability standard.
does_not_support: Use in higher education.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education (Ellucian 2026 AI report)
author: Ellucian
supports: Institutional AI use 66% (49% in 2024); 36% of Marketing, Admissions and Enrollment respondents use chatbots for FAQs; data security/privacy is the top institutional barrier (56%); 14% of executive respondents report a dedicated AI budget. No share for AI agents is reported.
does_not_support: Representativeness (vendor customers and contacts); agentic use.

title: Survey: Higher Ed AI Adoption Faces Financial, Policy Hurdles (EDUCAUSE 2025 AI Landscape Study)
author: GovTech reporting EDUCAUSE
type: secondary report of an association survey
supports: 57% say AI is a strategic priority; 39% have AI acceptable-use policies; only 9% say privacy/security policies adequately address AI; only 2% fund AI with new sources; a 'widening digital divide' with larger institutions ahead.
does_not_support: Admissions-specific or agent-specific adoption; secondary report.

title: UPCEA-EducationDynamics AI Readiness Report 2025
author: UPCEA and EducationDynamics
supports: Marketing and enrollment staff in online/professional education: 36% feel behind peers, 21% ahead; 56% do not see their institution as an AI leader; 79% expect chatbots/virtual assistants to transform marketing and enrollment within two years; barriers: budget 76%, technical infrastructure 64%, data privacy 52%, staff readiness 50%. Agents are not mentioned.
does_not_support: A peer-group adoption rate; the sample is too small and self-selected.

title: Unity Environmental University taps Agentforce and Education Cloud
author: Salesforce
supports: A university planned to deploy recruitment agents on its website to answer prospective-student questions, handle requests for information and guide applications, with hand-off to staff; it expected to save $800 of staff time per web RFI.
does_not_support: Measured results; the deployment was planned at publication and the savings are a projection.

title: Agentforce for Education: Recruitment and Admissions pre-built skill; Dreamforce 2025 education keynote summary
author: Salesforce; Cloud for Good (partner)
type: vendor product page and partner summary
supports: A pre-built recruitment/admissions agent skill exists (answer questions from knowledge articles, create information requests, register campus tours, start applications); partner summary lists recruitment and RFI skills as generally available with some items in beta. This is change-agent activity that raises trialability.
does_not_support: Customer counts or outcomes; the product page itself warns features 'may not be currently available'.

title: College of Professional Studies Increases Student Support Through Artificial Intelligence Chatbot
author: Syracuse University College of Professional Studies
supports: A peer professional-studies school deployed an Ivy.ai FAQ chatbot ('Orange Bot') for current and prospective students, answering 24/7 in 105+ languages and routing prospects to admissions.
does_not_support: Agentic tool use or outcomes; one institution.

title: Meet the NYUAdmissionsBot
author: NYU Admissions
supports: NYU Admissions offers a generative AI admissions bot on its admissions site and applicant portal, available 24/7; it hands off to a live agent or a contact form when it cannot answer.
does_not_support: SPS graduate admissions specifically; agentic actions; vendor; usage.

title: NYU SPS Graduate Admissions
author: NYU School of Professional Studies
supports: Phone/email contact, weekday appointments, information sessions and 'For immediate assistance, try our chatbot, Violet.'
does_not_support: Violet's architecture, tool use, vendor or usage.

title: How an Artificially Intelligent Virtual Assistant Helps Students Navigate the Road to College
author: Lindsay C. Page and Hunter Gehlbach
supports: A pre-LLM conversational assistant supported pre-enrollment tasks at Georgia State: chatbots in admissions-adjacent work date back to the innovator stage around 2016.
does_not_support: LLM agents; current adoption.

title: Colleges use AI in admissions (Intelligent.com survey reported by eCampus News)
author: eCampus News reporting Intelligent.com
type: commercial survey, recruitment method not disclosed
supports: 399 'education professionals' (79% higher education, 21% private high schools): 56% say their school uses AI in admissions and 82% expect to by 2024; uses: reviewing recommendation letters 73%, transcripts 71%, communicating with applicants 61%.
does_not_support: A current or representative adoption rate; agentic recruitment support. Stale (2023), mixed population, undisclosed sampling, and mostly about reviewing documents.
